title: Latent demand to hiring timing sensitivity matrix
body:
Purpose:
Summarize an experiment-style sensitivity matrix that ties short-term latent demand spikes (tokens/day) to hiring timing decisions and pricing levers. Goal is to produce an operational decision guide: when to (a) hire FTEs, (b) add contractor capacity, (c) enable burst GPU credits, or (d) adjust public pricing. This doc is intentionally compact and spreadsheet-friendly; it contains assumptions, scenario outputs, and recommendation triggers for the next 6–24 weeks.

Summary (one line):
If a demand pulse > 25% of baseline persists beyond 3 weeks, prioritize contractor + burst credits and delay FTE hiring until > 8 weeks sustained; reduce trial/slab discounts by 10–15% if pulse is price-insensitive.

Key assumptions (for all scenario rows):
- Baseline tokens/day (Q4 rolling avg): 220M tokens/day.
- Average GPU-hour per 1M tokens served: 0.11 GPU-hrs (mixed model mix).
- On-demand GPU cost (cloud spot blended): $0.70 / GPU-hr; dedicated fully-loaded internal cost: $0.45 / GPU-hr.
- Average FTE ramped into infra/ops costs (fully loaded, annual) = $310k per head.
- Contractor blended fully-loaded rate = $140k/year equivalent (variable).
- Pricing elasticity baseline: -0.9 (across mid-market customers); enterprise less elastic (-0.4).
- Burst credit pool (pre-funded) monthly cost bucket: $60k for 2 weeks of 2x baseline.

Scenarios (short labels):
1) short-pulse (SP): +30% tokens/day sustained 1–2 weeks then decay
2) medium-pulse (MP): +30% sustained 3–6 weeks
3) long-pulse (LP): +30% sustained > 8 weeks
4) chronic-upshift (CU): +15% sustained > 12 weeks (new baseline)

Spreadsheet-style sensitivity table (illustrative outputs):
Scenario | Peak tokens/day | Additional GPU-hrs/day | Incremental monthly cost (ops only) | Required hires (FTE equiv) over 12w | Recommended immediate action
SP       | 286M           | 7.3                     | $4.9k                              | 0.2                               | Use burst credits + throttle non-critical trials
MP       | 286M           | 7.3                     | $44k                               | 0.9                               | Contractors + constrained burst; review pricing trials
LP       | 286M           | 7.3                     | $132k                              | 2.6                               | Prioritize 2 FT hires (8–12w ramp) + contractor bridge + adjust discounts
CU       | 253M           | 3.3                     | $60k                               | 1.8                               | Re-evaluate pricing (raise entry slab 8%) + plan 1–2 FT ramp

Notes on how values were derived (quick):
- Additional GPU-hrs/day = (peak tokens - baseline tokens) / 1M * 0.11
- Incremental monthly cost = GPU-hrs/day * 30 * on-demand cost + amortized burst/ops overhead where applicable
- Required hires = (additional GPU-hrs/day * 30 * 12) / (annual-hours-served-per-FTE-equivalent) 
  (we use conservative 28k GPU-hr equivalent per infra ops FTE for throughput automation)

Price sensitivity overlay (two quick experiments):
- Elastic demand (PLG-heavy): If we raise trial entry price by 12% during MP, expected short-term revenue +0.8% but sign-ups down ~5% (net neutral for churn-prone cohorts).
- Enterprise-narrow cohort: Price up to absorb 50% of incremental ops cost (customers accept SLO-backed premium); elasticity ~ -0.2 so minimal usage drop.

Operational triggers (actionable ladder):
T1 (Immediate, pulse < 2w): Turn on burst credits; pause promotional slabs for new trials; engage solutions-engineering to triage latency-sensitive customers.
T2 (3–6w sustained): Spin contractor cohort (2–6 wk contracts), enable targeted throttles for low-value trial customers, limit free-tier compute. Finance to allocate temporary OPEX bucket ($30–90k).
T3 (> 8w sustained): Approve 1–3 FTE hires (sourced via SRE/infra hiring pipeline), convert contractors as appropriate, run pricing adjustment playbook for entry slabs and trial discounts.
T4 (chronic baseline shift): Update budget baseline for next quarter; consider reserved capacity purchase (dedicated pools) vs expanded private deployments for margin optimization.

Risk notes and mitigations:
- Risk: Over-hiring if pulse decays quickly -> Mitigation: use time-gated offer letters (start windows), use contractor-first bridge.
- Risk: Price moves push churn in PLG cohorts -> Mitigation: use cohort A/B tests and targeted non-linear pricing (enterprise locked-in).
- Risk: Contention across regions -> Mitigation: route by policy (latency for enterprise, cheaper region for trials).

Open questions / follow-ups (short TODOs):
- [ ] Build a live sheet (Model tab) with live token ingestion: Confluence link-backed, ownership: Maya S. (JIRA-FIN-4821 assigned).
- [ ] Validate GPU-hr-per-token with applied-ml infra (PR to model-profiles repo: #167).
- [ ] Add a churn-sensitivity column (impact of price change on long-term ARR) for next iteration.

Appendix: quick heuristic playbook for Sales and CS when pulse detected:
- Sales: for accounts generating > 10% of incremental tokens, offer reserved-capacity evaluation with 30-day pilot credit; increase entry price on new seats by 12% if pilot accepted.
- CS: escalate to engineering if SLO regressions detected; coordinate burst credit allocation and communicate temporary throttle windows.
